anti_generic_signature_read: 'Planet pieces with distinct surface markings, ranked by size and numbered, instead of generic tokens. Two colour-coded sets whose copies differ from each other. Themed terrain tiles with spikes and craters. Matching storage trays.'
blind_action_read: 'Players place pieces on grid squares and move them, as in a two-player strategy game. None of the pieces have moving parts. The trays appear to store one full 8-piece set each.'
blind_form_read: 'Each is a sphere on a short collar, on a disc base... Surface markings: bands, spots and continents are mostly flat colour inlays, with no relief. Rings: the ringed planets carry true raised ring geometry.'
blind_held_read: 'It is a tabletop board game... Playing pieces: 16 of them. Each is a coloured ball, shaped like a planet, sitting on a round disc base. A person would pick up and move the planet pieces.'
blind_relationship_read: 'There are two sets of 8 pieces: one on white bases and one on black bases... Sphere sizes step down from Jupiter (largest) to the grey cratered world'; 'The two copies are mirror images'; and, before any intent was known, a small ellipse 'directly below the oval... roughly 1/3 of the oval's width... a clear blue strip... separates it'.
blind_subjects_read: Named cold from colour and markings: Jupiter (bands, red spot), Saturn (disc ring), Uranus ('plain cyan with a thin vertical ring'), Neptune ('deep blue with thin white bands and a grey oval'), Earth, Venus, Mars, and a grey cratered world (Mercury or the Moon); base digits match planet size.

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: Round 1 (blind), black-base copy: 'A small grey spot below the oval, fully visible'; round 1 found the white-base copy's 'mostly hidden by the collar' and called it blocking, so it was moved. Round 2 fresh read: 'Complete and uncovered on both (images 5, 7, 20 for white-base; 6, 8, 21 for black-base).'
critical_form_requirements.requirement: R1. The bright companion cloud is added on BOTH Neptune pieces.

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: Blind narrow re-read of the lit frames before reveal: '(b) and (c) are tied as the lightest; both are white... (b) now matches (c), not (a)'; 'bright white' in images 20 and 21. In the shaded level frames it reads mid grey, which the critic attributed to lighting; the sealed filament is white #FFFEF7.
Round 1 blind: 'a single closed ellipse, about 1.8:1' (image 21). Round 2 fresh: 'A single closed ellipse on both. It is no longer truncated.'
critical_form_requirements.requirement: R3. It is one outline oval: a single closed ellipse, not a crescent, streak or band.

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: Round 1 blind: 'about 42x18 px, an aspect ratio of about 2.3:1... roughly 1/3 of the oval's width'. Round 2 fresh: 'about 2:1 and 0.38 of the spot on white-base; about 2.2:1 and 0.35 on black-base.' Measured on the solid: 9.99 by 5.00 degrees of arc.
critical_form_requirements.requirement: R4. About 10 by 5 degrees of arc: roughly 2:1 and about a third of the 28-degree-wide dark spot.

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: Round 1 blind, before any intent was known: 'directly below the oval, offset slightly right of the oval's centre... a clear blue strip... separates it'. Round 2 fresh, disclosed re-review: 'it still reads as a companion hugging the spot's southern side, since it is well inside the spot's east-west span'; it sits 'under the western half... It fails the brief's same longitude as written'. The departure and its reason are sealed in the limitations.
critical_form_requirements.requirement: R5. Just south of the Great Dark Spot. Brief: centred about 8 deg south at the same longitude; built 11.5 deg south and 10 deg west, inside the spot's east-west span, because 8 south overlaps the spot and the spot's own meridian buries 41% of it under the Sol collar. The longitude departure is disclosed, not waived.

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: Round 1 blind: 'a clear blue strip of about 7 px separates it from the oval, so they do not touch'. Round 2 fresh: 'Clear blue gaps of about 15-18 px in the lit views... clear of bands and collar, with no sliver or cut edge.' Measured: 0.526 mm to the spot at the inlay floor, 0.954 mm to the bands, minor axis 0.955 mm.
critical_form_requirements.requirement: R6. Inside the set's narrowest-feature limit (0.40 mm for any marking or bare gap): no sliver, a blue gap to the spot, touching no other marking.

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: Round 2: 'The spot, bands, globe, collar and base look the same as round 1' (visual recall). Measured on the built bodies against a rebuild of the source: spot, bands, disc and numeral identical in volume and bounding box on both armies; globe lost exactly the companion's volume; render diff changed only at the companion; opposite and polar frames pixel-identical.
critical_form_requirements.requirement: R7. NEGATIVE: nothing else on either Neptune piece changes (dark spot, three bands, globe, base, numeral).

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: Round 2: 'Images 1 and 2 look identical to round 1.' Measured: all 24 printed parts rebuild to the source's exact B-rep identity; the assembly gains exactly the two companion occurrences (220 -> 222); the render diff shows no change off Neptune beyond antialiasing specks on thin cone silhouettes.
critical_form_requirements.requirement: R8. NEGATIVE: nothing on any other part changes.

largest_risk: The critic's round-1 answer: 'the fine detail, above all the thin Uranus ring and the hairline Neptune bands and small spot, which may break, fail to print, or end up hidden by the collar.' The collar part was this correction's fault and was repaired; the rest is pre-existing and unchanged.
resolution: Round 1 found the companion fully present on the Anti-Sol piece but 41% under the seat collar on the Sol piece and called that blocking; it also read the companion grey in the shaded frames. Repair 1 moved the companion 10 deg west (to -33.5, -75.2) so it clears the collar on both armies with a 0.526 mm gap to the spot, and added two lit frames that show it white. Round 2, disclosed, recorded fresh observations first and found no blocking defect; the same-longitude departure is stated in R5 and the limitations.
reviewer: One independent native critic, two rounds: round 1 unprimed on the canonical renders; round 2 a disclosed re-review after one repair, fresh observations recorded first.
